chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from some of our companions, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: I have been informed that some people go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) carrying different kinds of food with them, including Akhbisah and other similar deserts. Verily if they had gone to the graves of their loved ones, they would not have taken such things with them.

key_terms.الْأَخْبِصَةُ: Akbisah, a type of sweet bread or pastry
key_terms.الْحَلَاوَةُ: Halaweh, a sweet confection or dessert
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), the grandson of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What food items are traditionally carried during the Ziyarah of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) observes that devotees carry specific delicacies like ḥalāwah and akhbisah to the shrine of Ḥusain (a.s.), a practice not typically extended to ordinary graves, highlighting the unique status of the Imams as recipients of honor and sustenance. This distinction underscores the theological concept of the Ahl al-Bayt’s spiritual authority and the communal act of sharing blessings (barakah) with the righteous, elevating their graves beyond mere burial sites to centers of spiritual connection.
